Phase 1 confirmed a two-part incomplete implementation in the handwritten MCP adapter. E1 built the real server and inspected both the registered callable and live FastMCP schema in the same process: signature `(id1, id2)` and schema properties `{id1,id2}` both omitted `relation`, ruling out stale client/server cache. E2 drove a real MCP unlink against an ephemeral pair holding `blocks` then `relates_to`: the runtime spy recorded exactly two positional arguments, MCP removed the newest `relates_to` edge, while the library control `rebar.unlink(a,b,"blocks")` removed only `blocks`. E3 temporarily added only the optional callable parameter while deliberately leaving the two-argument delegate unchanged: the live schema then accepted `relation="blocks"`, but the spy still recorded only `(a,b)` and MCP still removed `relates_to`; instrumentation was removed and the worktree is clean.

Root cause: `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py::unlink_tickets` independently omits the already-supported optional relation selector from both its registered signature and its `rebar.unlink` call. Both omissions are necessary to explain the inability to express the selector and the pair-scoped fallback at runtime. Defect legitimacy is `incomplete-implementation`: the signed final ruling on restoring-shallow-blobfish requires zero intended write-parameter divergences and total lib/CLI/MCP parity; relation-scoped unlink is already authoritative in docs/user-guide.md, docs/cli-reference.md, core/library code, and tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_unlink_relation_scoped_e39f.py. The older ticket-model prose and commit 73abb580 only record the earlier change scope, not a permanent divergence. Expected behavior: an explicit MCP relation removes exactly that edge; omission preserves pair-scoped most-recent behavior.
